subject: Re: Follow-up on deployment choice and data isolation for FinSecure

Subject: Follow-up: deployment options & data isolation — FinSecure

Hi Lena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared view.

Recap of what you described:
- Primary workload: customer support automation and transaction risk scoring that touches payment data and customer PII.
- Regulatory posture: PCI-adjacent controls, internal requirement for strict network isolation and auditability.
- Traffic profile: bursty QPS during business hours, target 50–200 rps peak for scoring calls, low-latency requirement (~100–250ms p95).
- Preference expressed: leaning away from public multi-tenant hosted API because of isolation concerns; evaluating Dedicated vs Private VPC or on-prem.

Key questions we need you to confirm (so Mateo can validate technically):
1) Is "data must never leave customer-owned network" a hard requirement, or is it acceptable for data to traverse a private peering link to a managed environment (i.e., Private VPC) if logs/audit and encryption controls are in place?
2) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM (CMEK) for any persisted artifacts (logs, cache, model snapshots)?
3) Is physical separation of GPU hardware required, or will single-tenant Dedicated pools (isolated capacity within Redwood) suffice?

Attachments: I attached the notes you sent in the call and our standard deployment summary for quick reference (finsecure-deployment-needs.pdf).

Next steps proposed:
- Mateo to follow up with a short technical note comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC against the three isolation pillars above. (ETA: 48 business hours)
- If Private VPC looks viable, propose a 2-week Private PoC spec (network diagram, control-plane options, required IP ranges).
- Schedule a short procurement call once we align on whether Private VPC is required.

If you can confirm answers to the three questions above, we’ll prioritize the technical write-up and a cost estimate.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and a couple of clarifications from our side:

Answers to your three questions:
1) Hard requirement: our security team prefers that customer data does not traverse any public network. Private peering (Direct Connect / PrivateLink style) into vendor-managed infra is acceptable only if we retain strict control over keys, traffic egress, and logging.
2) Yes, customer-managed KMS (CMEK) required for any persisted data or cache. We also need proof that KMS keys are never escrowed or accessible by vendor operators.
3) Physical GPU separation — preferred but not mandatory. The absolute must-haves are: single-tenant network path, no shared disk volumes with other customers, and strong KV cache lifecycle guarantees (no cross-tenant cache leakage).

I uploaded a short spreadsheet with our formal isolation checklist (data_isolation_requirements.xlsx). Procurement (Oliver) is on cc and will start documentation for an NDA + SOW once we have a recommended path.

One subtle thing: we will need per-request audit traces that map back to a request id and include a flag when any prompt touches PII. Is that something you can capture in your logs and make available via an audit API?

Happy to jump on a quick technical call if Mateo wants to walk through our checklist.

— Lena

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment options & data isolation — FinSecure

Thanks Lena — clear requirements, appreciated. I pulled together a concise comparison and a suggested PoC approach below. High level first, then specifics against your checklist items.

High-level comparison (implications for your controls):
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity):
  * Pros: single-tenant GPU pools, predictable throughput, no noisy neighbors at GPU level.
  * Cons: control plane still Redwood-hosted; network egress still traverses our managed network unless you use a private peering option. We offer CMEK for persisted artifacts and strong audit logs.
- Private VPC (customer VPC + private control plane):
  * Pros: customer-controlled network boundary, private peering (no public Internet), optional private control plane deployment, full VPC isolation and dedicated subnetting. Supports CMEK and HSM integrations.
  * Cons: higher operational lead time and uplift; may require additional networking setup on your side.
- On-prem: full control, maximum isolation, but significant operational burden and longer lead time.

Technical mapping to your checklist:
1) Data never leaves customer-owned network:
   - Private VPC: achievable via AWS PrivateLink / Direct Connect and a private control-plane option. Data plane can be routed only over the peering; audit logs can be streamed to your S3/CloudWatch.
   - Dedicated: typically not full "never leaves" — even with private interconnect there are control-plane interactions; we can scope to minimize telemetry and use encrypted tunnels, but not the same as customer-owned network.
2) CMEK / HSM:
   - Supported in Private VPC and Dedicated for persisted data (logs, artifacts). We can support AWS KMS with customer-managed keys and HSM integrations for higher EKM security.
3) Physical GPU separation / cache lifecycle:
   - Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and we guarantee no shared disk volumes. For cache: we can provide per-tenant KV namespaces and strict TTL/zeroization options; for Private VPC we can add an in-customer subnet-level cache in front of the Redwood runtime if you require it.
4) Per-request audit traces & PII flagging:
   - We can emit request-level traces with request_id, routing decision, model variant, and a PII flag if you provide or approve a PII detector hook. Traces can be pushed to your logging endpoint or retained in your account in Private VPC.

Proposed PoC (two-week):
- Objective: demonstrate Private VPC flow with CMEK and per-request audit traces.
- Environment: 2 inference nodes (A40 / T4 equivalent), private peering, customer-provided KMS, streaming of audit logs to your S3 bucket.
- Deliverables: network diagram, small runbook, cost estimate, test harness for 1k sample requests including PII tagging.

Open items (need from your team):
- CIDR(s) for peering / preferred cloud region.
- Expected QPS shapes for PoC and sample payloads to tune batching.
- List of any legal/contractual controls beyond our standard DPA so we can scope SOW.

I’ll draft the short technical note and PoC spec and share by EOD Monday. If that timeline works I’ll include estimated lead times and a budgetary range for Private VPC and Dedicated options.

— Mateo
